incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert fired -> PD#INC-2026 routing-prod p95-latency > 400ms (2m)
jamal: acked. i'm on it, grabbing dashboards
anya: ack. i saw something in HA proxy metrics too, tagging
mike: thanks — do we have customer impact yet? any 5xxs?
jamal: quick look: 500s ~= baseline, error rate flat. it's latency-only spike
carla: i'm seeing a tiny spike in kv-cache miss rate around same time
jamal: running quick query on metrics
jamal: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le))
```
jamal: returns ~420ms at peak then drops to 120ms within 30s
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert auto-resolved (no action taken) — alert window closed
anya: auto-resolved — timeline looks like a 1m warmup blip
mike: can we confirm no downstream retries / user-facing retries? check tracing for any long traces
carla: checked traces for endpoints served by that route — no elevated span errors, a handful of extra latency traces but not user-visible failures
jamal: root cause hypothesis: cold KV cache on a small subset of routing hosts; we had a short rolling deploy earlier today that touched that pool
anya: yes saw deployment marker ~4204980000, about 3m before spike. logs show a brief cache population job also ran
mike: actionables: 1) adjust alert to avoid 1m warmups (increase evaluation window to 5m or add warmup suppression) 2) add kv-cache warmup metric as a group dimension 3) create follow-up ticket to investigate deploy sequencing
jamal: filing ticket now -> INF-3456 "routing latency warmup: noisy alert tuning" and assign to infra
oncall-rotation-bot: Handoff reminder: jamal will stay on until 09:00 PT then hand to anya
anya: noted. i'll follow up with infra to add a short-lived suppress rule for warmup windows
mike: marking as no_customer_impact; please add a short blameless note in the ticket and paste the key graphs
carla: pasted graphs in INF-3456 and included the short promql snippet + kube deploy IDs
jamal: closing thread here — keeping ticket open for the tuning work. thanks all :raised_hands:
incident-bot: Thread closed (auto-resolved alert).
